title: Official Sources and Verification Register
text:
Maintaining evidence
For an official claim, record organization, document title, version/revision, section, URL, and date verified. For an educational example, mark it fictional and explain its purpose. For a project decision, record rationale, reviewer, and protocol version. Unresolved discrepancies belong in the variable map and should be resolved with the responsible expert before analysis.
No official manual, complete coding table, licensed stage definition, or patient record is bundled with this guide.

title: Sensitivity Analyses
text:
Note



Teaching outline; the template deliberately requires a study-specific implementation.

title: Sensitivity Analyses
text:
Challenge a named assumption
A sensitivity analysis asks whether a conclusion depends on a defensible alternative assumption. Examples include an alternate coding-era restriction, a different exposure definition, a justified missing-data approach, or an analysis addressing treatment timing.
For each analysis record the assumption, changed rule, target population/estimand, expected change in sample, and comparison to the primary result. Compare effect sizes, confidence intervals and cohort composition. A change in statistical significance alone is not a robustness criterion.
Prespecify the main alternatives and label exploratory additions. Do not cycle through exclusions to obtain a preferred p-value. Unmeasured confounding, immortal time and structural unavailability require design-specific expertise; a generic loop over models will not solve them.

title: Missingness and Data Quality
text:
Note



Teaching outline. Use release-specific definitions before creating analytic missing values.

title: Missingness and Data Quality
text:
Audit in layers
Start with raw-code frequencies and valid-value checks, then distinguish unknown, not applicable, not collected, suppressed and ordinary blank values where your dictionary supports those meanings. Python’s isna() sees software missing values; it does not know registry conventions.
Inspect availability and missingness by diagnosis year, disease scope and exposure group. Check ranges, timing consistency and unexpected categories. Keep an explicit reason field when multiple raw codes become analytic missing. Exact duplicate rows are a signal to investigate identity and import behavior, not automatic permission to delete.

title: Missingness and Data Quality
text:
Document the analysis denominator
Write down input N, exclusions and reasons, final N and events for each model. Complete-case analysis can change the population and introduce bias. Imputation cannot manufacture a historically uncollected construct without substantial assumptions. Choose and review the missing-data strategy before fitting; model helpers refuse missing input so this decision cannot be hidden by default deletion.
The dictionary lesson provides the map and availability workflow.

title: 4. Understanding and Navigating the Data Dictionary
section: Search by concept, then by exact variable
text:
Search by concept, then by exact variable
Educational explanation. Suppose your question includes “stage.” That word alone is insufficient: you may need clinical stage before treatment, pathologic stage after surgery, or another defined staging construct. A convenient column name does not settle the scientific question.

Write the concept and when it should be measured relative to the exposure.
Search the dictionary using the concept and likely synonyms. Read the whole item entry, including notes and related fields.
Record the exact raw name and item identifier, where available. Do not rename raw columns in place.
Check which cases and diagnosis years the item applies to. Look for changes in definition, coding system, collection requirements, and missing-value conventions.
Identify each possible raw value’s meaning using your local documentation. Keep code-like fields as strings during import.
Read the matching release changes and linked coding resources. A different manual’s similarly named item may have a different purpose.
Write your proposed analytic transformation separately; request mentor or registrar review where the meaning is unresolved.
After authorized import, compare actual codes and year-specific frequencies with expectations. Unexpected values should trigger investigation, not automatic coercion.

A variable map is an analysis contract

Field group

Source evidence

Scope

title: 4. Understanding and Navigating the Data Dictionary
text:
Worked example: fictional codes
Assume an invented field DEMO_MARKER uses P for present, A for absent, U for unknown, and N for not applicable. These are not NCDB codes.
Your source notes preserve all four meanings. A project decision might produce marker_present with 1 for P, 0 for A, and missing for the other two. Keep a companion reason field so U and N remain distinguishable. Mapping both to numeric missing is not permission to forget their different denominators.
import pandas as pd
raw = pd.Series(["P", "A", "U", "N"], dtype="string")
assert raw.isin(["P", "A", "U", "N"]).all()
analytic = raw.map({"P": 1, "A": 0}).astype("Int64")
reason = raw.map({"U": "unknown", "N": "not applicable"})
If a new value X appears, stop and establish its meaning. Do not convert every unrecognized code to missing silently.
crumbs: 4. Understanding and Navigating the Data Dictionary

title: 4. Understanding and Navigating the Data Dictionary
text:
Build an availability matrix
For each required field, make a row for each diagnosis year or documented era. Distinguish collected and applicable, not collected, not applicable, and uncertain. Then inspect observed missingness within the applicable cases. An empty column before collection began is structural unavailability; it is not ordinary sporadic missingness.
Project decision. If the exposure is unavailable for part of the proposed period, choose a justified restriction, a documented harmonization, or a revised question. Do not invent an equivalent field or impute an unmeasured historical construct without methodological review.

Ask another student to reproduce the decision from your notes. You are ready when they can distinguish official meaning from your analytic choice.

title: Data Protection and Safe Sharing
text:
This guide contains original text, source code, blank metadata templates and invented examples. Keep actual NCDB records in institution-approved storage outside the guide. Patient-level derived tables, predictions, matched cohorts, imputation files, model objects, notebooks, logs and screenshots can be sensitive too.
The .gitignore blocks common data formats, archives, credentials, environments, website output and generated projects. Only named blank CSV metadata templates are exempted. Do not turn those templates into patient tables. .gitignore does not remove already-tracked files and can be bypassed with force-add; it is one guard, not a security boundary.

title: Data Protection and Safe Sharing
text:
Before a commit
After staging, run python tools/check_repository.py from the guide root. It checks the Git index, including staged content, and blocks common risky formats, local paths, oversized files and some credential patterns. Review git diff --cached and git diff --cached --stat locally. Never paste a diff containing data into a public review tool.
For a folder without Git metadata, python tools/check_repository.py --source-tree checks source files while excluding local/generated directories. It is not a full disk audit. The tool cannot recognize every secret, patient record hidden in text, or disclosure through aggregate results.
To enable the included local pre-commit hook after initializing Git:
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
Run commits from an environment where python resolves to your project interpreter. Hooks can be bypassed; the included CI guard provides a second check, not authorization to upload records.

title: Data Protection and Safe Sharing
text:
Publication needs a separate review






NoteOfficial source — verify your agreement



The current PUF FAQ discusses restrictions on reporting small cells and the need to prevent reconstruction. Apply your executed agreement and institutional requirements; an example threshold in code is not the governing rule.


Educational explanation. If a total is 100 and one visible category is 97, hiding the other category does not hide its count of 3. Percentages, margins, complementary categories, repeated tables and KM risk tables can reveal counts. The suppression helper only formats one count and requires an explicit threshold. It does not perform complementary suppression or certify a table.
Project decision. Name a reviewer, applicable rule, approved output destination, and review date. Publish only cleared aggregate artifacts. Do not publish the entire analysis directory or its generated project.

title: Data Protection and Safe Sharing
section: If data were staged or shared
text:
If data were staged or shared
Stop the commit/upload. Keep incident details in approved channels and notify the responsible PI/privacy or security team. Removing a file from the working tree does not remove history, remote copies, logs or backups. Follow institutional incident procedures; do not attempt an undocumented history rewrite or claim that a deleted file has been recalled.

title: 5. Coding Systems
text: Recognize which reference answers which coding question and avoid treating different years, staging contexts, and tumor schemas as interchangeable.

title: 5. Coding Systems
text: Recognize which reference answers which coding question and avoid treating different years, staging contexts, and tumor schemas as interchangeable.

title: 5. Coding Systems
text:
A code needs a context
Educational explanation. A value has meaning only together with its field, disease context, coding version, and diagnosis year. Codes are labels unless the definition establishes a quantitative scale. For example, a treatment category numbered 3 is not necessarily “three times” category 1.








System or resource
Question it helps answer
What you must verify




ICD-O topography
Where did the primary tumor arise?
Applicable site code and version


ICD-O morphology
What tumor type and behavior were recorded?
Histology, behavior, and site compatibility


AJCC stage
What extent of disease is represented?
Disease schema, edition, clinical/pathologic context, timing


STORE / historical FORDS
How were registry items collected?
Diagnosis-year manual and whether the item is in your PUF


Collaborative Stage / SSFs
What did an older site-specific factor mean?
Schema, factor number, year, and definition


SSDI and grade manuals
What do site-specific or grade items mean?
Applicable schema, manual version, timing, and availability


SEER*Rx
How is a drug classified for registry coding?
Applicable guidance; do not infer patient regimen detail



Official starting points: SEER ICD-O materials, SEER introduction to site and morphology, ACS registry manuals, and the coding-resource links on the ACS PUF page.

title: 5. Coding Systems
text:
Site is not histology
Topography describes location; histology describes tumor type. Neither alone necessarily identifies the cohort you want. Review the official organ-site groupings and your disease-specific definition before filtering. A file’s name is a starting point for investigation, not a complete eligibility rule.
ICD-O is not interchangeable with ICD-10 diagnosis billing codes. SEER’s ICD-O materials also identify diagnosis-year changes in site–morphology validation resources. Do not apply a current validation table to every historical year without checking applicability.

title: 5. Coding Systems
section: Stage is more than a number
text:
Stage is more than a number
Clinical and pathologic assessments use different information at different points in care. A postoperative assessment can be affected by treatment and selection into surgery. Substituting it for baseline disease severity can change the scientific interpretation of a model.
Project decision. State the intended stage construct, required timing, precedence rule if multiple fields exist, and approach to discordance. Retain the original fields and a flag identifying the source used. If two staging editions differ, do not assume that identical labels represent identical disease severity. A universal conversion table is not supplied here.
Use the release dictionary and linked AJCC resources to verify the edition and schema. This guide does not reproduce licensed staging tables.

title: 5. Coding Systems
text:
Changing site-specific fields
A historical numbered site-specific factor and a newer named item may both sound like a biomarker, yet differ in definition, specimen context, collection years, or codes. Check source meaning before combining them. Document a separate transformation for each supported era; otherwise label the era unavailable or restrict the study with a rationale.

title: 5. Coding Systems
text:
Treatment and grade
Distinguish treatment at the reporting facility from summary treatment where your fields make that distinction. Do not convert a treatment summary into dose, regimen, adherence, or recurrence treatment detail that it does not contain. Likewise, distinguish grade context before combining columns. The correct recode depends on the item and disease, not a generic number range.

title: 5. Coding Systems
section: Practice: the same code in two eras
text:
Practice: the same code in two eras
In an invented dataset, era A uses 1 = marker present; era B uses 1 = test not performed. A naive merge would combine incompatible categories. Write two mapping rules and a reason for every missing value. Then explain why looking only at the distribution of 1 cannot detect this mistake.

title: 5. Coding Systems
text:
Readiness check
For one planned field, identify its coding resource, version, disease scope, years, and timing. If any is unknown, put the uncertainty in your variable map before analysis. Next: Computer Setup.

title: Analysis Overview
text:
Use an explicit sequence
Define the question and protocol → verify variables → import and audit → build the cohort → recode → inspect missingness and Table 1 → implement the approved primary analysis → assess diagnostics → run prespecified sensitivities → review outputs and reporting.
Real-data model helpers do not select covariates, drop missing rows, tune definitions or publish results. Facility clustering, missing-data alternatives, causal estimands and treatment timing require additional study-specific implementation and expert review.

title: 2. Obtaining Access
text:
Who does what?
Educational explanation. Start by identifying people, not by downloading software.







Role
Practical preparation task




Faculty principal investigator (PI)
Own the proposal, verify eligibility, and complete required agreements


Student or researcher
Draft feasibility notes, learn the dictionary, and document the workflow


Cancer registrar / QPort contact
Help identify the correct program contact and application access route


Analyst or statistician
Assess data feasibility, design, resources, and analysis requirements


Institutional research/privacy office
Determine local review, storage, access, and retention requirements



Being a student at a hospital does not automatically authorize downloading or analyzing its PUF. Work through the PI’s approved team and access process.

title: 2. Obtaining Access
text:
Prepare a small application packet

Draft the population, exposure, comparator, and outcome in plain language.
Verify that the requested organ-site file and diagnosis years can support the question. A familiar disease label is not a substitute for checking file groupings.
List required fields and unresolved coding questions in your variable map.
Explain the primary analysis, missing-data plan, and principal limitations. Have a mentor assess whether the question is feasible.
Assemble personnel information and supporting materials using the current official checklist. Keep biosketches and application records in approved local storage.
Ask the QPort contact to confirm the PI’s applicant designation; then follow the official portal workflow.
Record approval and download notifications, applicable agreements, and the permitted users before obtaining the files.

The current FAQ restricts data access outside the facility and describes how to update investigators. A collaborator’s expertise is not permission to send them data. Resolve team changes with the PI and NCDB.

title: 2. Obtaining Access
section: Institutional review is a separate step
text:
Institutional review is a separate step
Project decision. Obtain your institution’s determination about IRB or other research review. Do not copy another paper’s “exempt” or “not human subjects research” statement into your protocol. Record the actual determination, date, reference number, and any conditions locally.
Agree where files may reside, who may access them, how backups work, and what happens when a student graduates. Use institutional channels for credentials; do not save passwords in Python, YAML, Markdown, or Git.

title: 2. Obtaining Access
text:
Your access record
In approved local storage, maintain a short record with: PI and analyst; authorized team; project purpose; approved file/site; approval reference; storage owner; permitted storage location; training completion; download deadline from the notification; and retention/handoff obligations. The reusable template contains access_record.md with blank fields.

title: 2. Obtaining Access
text:
If access does not work
Confirm the applicant role with the institutional contact. Follow official password recovery. Do not borrow another person’s login. A download archive may use a different password from the portal; follow the instructions supplied with that download.

title: 2. Obtaining Access
text:
Practice and readiness
Write a draft email to your mentor identifying the institutional contact, your question, and three unresolved feasibility items. You do not need to send it to complete the lesson. You are ready for the next step when you can identify the PI, access route, local review process, and approved storage owner.

Still waiting for access? Complete the foundations and synthetic walkthrough. All practice records are invented.
Have approved data? Start with the import plan, variable map, and cohort definition. Keep records in approved institutional storage outside this guide.

This repository holds code, original teaching material, and synthetic examples only. title: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files
text:
Three different dates
Educational explanation. A diagnosis year belongs to a case. A PUF release identifies an edition of the extract. A download date records when your team obtained it. They are not interchangeable. A recently downloaded release can contain many earlier diagnosis years, and those years do not guarantee every field was collected throughout.

title: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files
text:
Inventory before opening data








Item
Purpose
What to record locally




Compressed/encrypted download
Delivery container
Original filename, release, byte size, download date


Extracted text data
Case records
Exact path, checksum, file size; keep unchanged


Layout / import script
Positions, types, names, and labels
Release match and script version


PUF dictionary
Meanings, valid codes, availability, notes
Title, revision date, item references


Getting Started and changes notes

Applicable version and issues for your study


Local analysis outputs
Your transformations
Input checksum, code version, run date



The project template supplies a blank file_manifest.csv. A checksum is a file fingerprint: it helps detect accidental changes, but it does not prove that a file is complete or scientifically valid. Keep manifests describing restricted downloads with the local project.
crumbs: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files

title: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files
text:
Why double-clicking is not importing
A text file may use fixed positions rather than commas. In a fixed-width layout, a field occupies a defined character interval. An incorrect interval can produce plausible-looking but incorrect values without raising an error. Leading zeros can disappear if codes become integers.
The official 2024 Quick Start Data Structure supplies release-specific layout information. This guide intentionally does not reproduce that layout. Follow the synthetic walkthrough to learn position conversion with invented fields.
For a real parser, reconcile the supplied positions, field lengths, types, encoding, and record length. Validate a small authorized local sample against the supplied import method before processing the whole file. Never use a screenshot or copied patient row to ask for help here.
crumbs: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files

title: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files
text:
Cases, identifiers, and releases
The 2024 Getting Started document describes randomly assigned case identifiers that change between releases and cannot link cases across cancer sites. The FAQ advises against combining old and new PUF versions.
Educational explanation. Do not append a newer release to an older one to “add another year.” Repeated records and updated information can change counts and estimates. Treat each release as a separately documented input. Do not assume one case equals a uniquely linkable person across files.
crumbs: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files

title: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files
text:
Storage plan
Keep real raw files read-only in approved institutional storage outside this repository. Keep processed patient-level files, logs, plots awaiting disclosure review, and model objects there too. A Parquet file is still patient-level data when it contains one row per case. De-identification does not make redistribution appropriate.
Project decision. Document a local data path, release, checksums, and parser version. The generated project’s config.local.yaml is ignored; its portable config.yaml has no real data path. Never place downloaded data under website/, where publication tools may copy it.
crumbs: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files

title: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files
text:
Practice and readiness
Without opening any real dataset, fill an inventory for an imaginary release and draw the route from text → validated table → cohort → model. Explain why the diagnosis-year range and variable-year range may differ. Continue to Navigating the Data Dictionary.
crumbs: 3. Understanding the PUF and Downloaded Files

title: Reproducibility and Project Handoff
text:
Note



Teaching outline. Adapt the handoff to institutional policy and your approved study.

title: Reproducibility and Project Handoff
text:
Reconstruct the work
Record the PUF release and local input checksums, dictionary revisions, protocol version, source-code commit, Python/package versions, Quarto version and run command. Keep patient-level inputs and outputs in approved storage. The public code should be understandable without copying those records.
Separate immutable inputs, intermediate transformations and reviewed aggregate results. Preserve a cohort flow and a record of changes to the protocol. A fixed random seed makes a computational step repeatable; it does not address biased study design.

title: Reproducibility and Project Handoff
text:
Hand off responsibility
Give the next authorized researcher the question, access requirements, approved storage location, environment instructions, variable map, cohort rules, analysis plan, diagnostics, disclosure review record and known limitations through approved channels. Test recreation using the synthetic demo. Re-run the real study only in the authorized environment.
Have the PI confirm access changes when a researcher leaves. Do not transfer credentials, copy data to personal storage, or assume access continues after graduation.

title: 6. Computer, VS Code, and Python Setup
text:
Know the tools
Educational explanation. Python runs analysis code. VS Code edits files and provides a terminal. A terminal accepts commands; it is not the Python prompt marked >>>. Git records source changes. Quarto converts .qmd lessons into a searchable website. Installing the Python package named quarto does not replace the Quarto CLI.
Use Python 3.11 for the tested environment. The dependency snapshot records an exact tested package set; other Python versions and operating systems require their own validation. Download installers from Python, VS Code, Git, and Quarto, following institutional software policy.

title: 6. Computer, VS Code, and Python Setup
text:
Open the right folder
In VS Code, choose File → Open Folder and select the guide folder containing requirements.txt, create_ncdb_project.py, and website. Open Terminal → New Terminal. Commands below assume that folder is your working directory. Do not type the Markdown backticks or the prompt symbol.

title: 6. Computer, VS Code, and Python Setup
text:
Create and install the environment
On macOS/Linux:
python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
On Windows PowerShell:
py -3.11 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
If activation is blocked by institutional policy, call the interpreter directly rather than changing that policy:
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
A virtual environment holds this project’s packages separately. Recreate it after moving the project; do not copy it or commit it. See Python’s venv documentation.

title: 6. Computer, VS Code, and Python Setup
section: Select the interpreter in VS Code
text:
Select the interpreter in VS Code
Install Microsoft’s Python extension. Open the Command Palette and run Python: Select Interpreter; select the Python inside this folder’s .venv. Open a fresh terminal. The VS Code environment guide documents interpreter selection and environment discovery.
python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable); print(sys.version)"
python -m pip check
python tools/check_environment.py
The executable should end in .venv/bin/python or .venv\Scripts\python.exe. pip check should report no broken requirements. If an import fails, compare the selected interpreter with the one printed above before reinstalling anything.

Build and search the guide
quarto --version
quarto render website
quarto preview website
A successful render produces website/_site/index.html and search.json. Preview starts a local server; open the address printed in the terminal and try searching “variable map.” Stop preview with Ctrl+C. The website displays code examples without executing analysis on render; executable practice is tested separately.
If this machine’s Quarto was installed locally during development, use the absolute CLI path recorded in AUDIT.md, or install the CLI normally from the official download page. Restart the terminal after installation if quarto is not found.

Run the synthetic practice project
python create_ncdb_project.py --name "Practice study" --site "Synthetic" --outcome "demo_event" --exposure "demo_group"
python projects/practice_study/scripts/run_synthetic.py
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
The generator creates a protected local project. The demo creates invented records in memory and writes only synthetic aggregate outputs into its ignored results/ folder. It does not read NCDB files. See the walkthrough for interpretation.

title: 6. Computer, VS Code, and Python Setup
text:
A few Python ideas
A variable names an object. A function packages a reusable operation. A pandas DataFrame is a table; a Series is a column. df["age"] selects a column; df.loc[mask] selects rows where a Boolean condition is true. Indentation defines blocks. A traceback ends with the immediate error, but the earlier lines show how execution reached it.

title: 1. Start Here: What is NCDB?
text:
By the end, you should be able to describe the data source, distinguish a case from a population denominator, and decide whether a proposed outcome is observable.






NoteOfficial source — verify



The National Cancer Database is a hospital-based registry program of the American College of Surgeons and the American Cancer Society. See the ACS NCDB overview. The PUF FAQ states that NCDB is not population-based, cannot support population incidence calculations, and that recurrence is not included in the PUF.

NoteOfficial source — verify



The National Cancer Database is a hospital-based registry program of the American College of Surgeons and the American Cancer Society. See the ACS NCDB overview. The PUF FAQ states that NCDB is not population-based, cannot support population incidence calculations, and that recurrence is not included in the PUF.

title: 1. Start Here: What is NCDB?
section: A registry is a structured account of care
text:
A registry is a structured account of care
Educational explanation. A cancer registry translates clinical information into standardized fields. A row represents a cancer case; a column represents an item such as diagnosis year or a treatment characteristic. A registry code is the output of a coding rule, not a complete clinical narrative. “Unknown” may reflect absent documentation rather than a patient’s underlying condition.
The Participant User File (PUF) is the research extract you apply to receive. It is not a live connection to hospital charts or the whole registry. The records you analyze have already passed through selection and processing before your study starts. Your analytic cohort adds another layer of selection.
Think of the study population as a sequence:
People with cancer → cases captured by contributing programs
→ cases included in your PUF release → cases meeting your protocol
→ cases with information required for a particular analysis
Each arrow can change who is represented. Large sample size does not eliminate selection bias.

title: 1. Start Here: What is NCDB?
text:
What questions fit?







Proposed question
Feasibility assessment




How does recorded treatment use differ across observed groups?
Potentially feasible after verifying treatment definitions and comparable years


Is an exposure associated with overall survival?
Potentially feasible with valid follow-up, time origin, confounders, and bias assessment


What is the national incidence of this cancer?
Not an appropriate NCDB PUF question: there is no population denominator


Does treatment prevent recurrence?
The required recurrence endpoint is unavailable in the PUF described by the current FAQ


Did treatment cause longer survival?
Observational comparisons require additional causal assumptions; a regression coefficient alone cannot establish this



Cancer-specific mortality is also unavailable according to the current application instructions. Do not rename overall survival as cancer-specific survival.

title: 1. Start Here: What is NCDB?
section: Turn an idea into a research question
text:
Turn an idea into a research question
Project decision. Write one sentence naming the population, exposure, comparator, outcome, and relevant time period. For example: “Among a prespecified eligible cancer cohort, is recorded treatment A associated with overall survival compared with treatment B?” This is a question template, not a recommended clinical comparison.
Now list what must be observable: eligibility before treatment, treatment definition and timing, outcome timing, baseline confounders, and follow-up. Mark each as verified, uncertain, or unavailable. An uncertain primary outcome is a feasibility problem to resolve before applying or modeling.
Do not select covariates simply because they are available. A confounder can influence both treatment selection and outcome; a mediator occurs along the pathway from treatment to outcome. Adjusting for these has different implications. Bring a timeline or causal diagram to your mentor.

title: 1. Start Here: What is NCDB?
text:
Practice: a five-minute feasibility note
Write your proposed question, the source population you can actually study, three required concepts, and one limitation that a larger sample would not solve. Find each concept in the release-specific dictionary. Stop at “not verified” when you cannot establish a definition.

title: 1. Start Here: What is NCDB?
text:
Readiness check
Can you explain why a million hospital cases do not provide a national incidence denominator? Can you name the endpoint your file actually measures? Can you distinguish association from a causal effect? If so, continue to Obtaining Access.

title: Synthetic Walkthrough
text: Practice a reproducible sequence before handling approved records. Every field beginning demo_ is invented; the distributions and model coefficients have no NCDB or clinical interpretation.

title: Synthetic Walkthrough
text: Practice a reproducible sequence before handling approved records. Every field beginning demo_ is invented; the distributions and model coefficients have no NCDB or clinical interpretation.

title: Synthetic Walkthrough
text:
Run it
From the guide root with the Python environment active:
python create_ncdb_project.py --name "Practice study" --site "Synthetic" --outcome "demo_event" --exposure "demo_group"
python projects/practice_study/scripts/run_synthetic.py
The generator refuses to overwrite an existing project. To repeat the practice analysis, run the second command again. Outputs are overwritten only in that project’s synthetic results folder.

title: Synthetic Walkthrough
text:
What happens

An in-memory fixed-width example uses invented ID, age, and marker fields. The first ID remains 001, demonstrating why codes should initially be strings.
A seeded random generator creates 600 fictional records with age, group, a separate binary outcome, and censored follow-up.
A fictional age restriction selects an adult practice cohort and records exclusions. This rule is not a recommendation for your study.
The script writes missingness summaries, grouped counts, logistic estimates, a KM plot, Cox estimates, and a small run summary.
Propensity scores are estimated to exercise the function, but no matching or causal effect is claimed. Individual scores and individual records are not exported.

title: Synthetic Walkthrough
text:
Learn fixed-width positions
Imagine 00145P: positions 1–3 are an invented identifier, 4–5 are age, and 6 is a fictional marker. Python’s colspecs use zero-based, end-exclusive positions: [(0, 3), (3, 5), (5, 6)]. The endpoint is not included. This example is not an NCDB layout. See pandas read_fwf.

title: Synthetic Walkthrough
text:
Inspect the outputs
Open projects/practice_study/results/synthetic/summary.json and cohort_flow.csv locally. Confirm that retained plus excluded equals 600. Check that Table 1 counts sum to the final cohort. The binary outcome used for logistic regression differs from the follow-up event used by survival models; they answer different demonstration questions.
The KM curve displays censoring-based estimates for invented groups. The logistic and Cox confidence intervals reflect fitted sampling models, not real clinical evidence. These estimates do not validate assumptions or authorize the same specification on NCDB data.

title: Synthetic Walkthrough
text:
Extend carefully
Change the synthetic seed and observe variation. Add a missing predictor and confirm that the model helper refuses it. Explain why that refusal requires a missing-data decision rather than an automatic .dropna(). Run tests again after changing utilities.
Next: use the analysis overview to plan a real study with your mentor.
